summary: Styles for the hand-built SVG, canvas and HTML charts: shared axis labels, the score histogram, horizontal bar lists, the semicircle risk gauge, the score waterfall, and the dot-matrix world map with its arcs, city markers, legend and stats strip. Most colours come from `var(--lvl)` on elements that carry a `lvl-` class; that works because these are CSS rules, whereas SVG presentation attributes don't reliably accept `var()`, which is why charts/core.js resolves tokens to real colours when it writes attributes.

notes.text: Section comment, then the axis labels of every SVG chart (the chart JS gives them `class="axis"`): 10px mono in the faintest grey. SVG text is coloured with `fill`, not `color`.
Chart containers span the full panel width and keep at least 60px of height before the chart JS has drawn into them.
Section comment, then the score histogram bars. Each `rect` has a `lvl-` class, so `fill: var(--lvl)` colours it by the level its score falls in; bars sit at 88% opacity with an opacity transition.
The hovered bar becomes fully opaque while the tooltip shows its count.
The histogram's baseline (the x-axis line) uses the stronger hairline colour.

The level thresholds (30, 60 and 80) are faint dashed vertical lines (`stroke-dasharray: 2 3` means 2px dash, 3px gap) labelled with small mono numbers, so you can see where LOW becomes MEDIUM and so on.
Section comment, then the horizontal bar list (Top signals, a customer's locations): a grid of rows 11px apart.

Each bar row is a two-column grid (a flexible label column and a 34px value column) with named areas: the first row is `"label value"` and the second `"track track"`, so the bar spans the full width underneath.
The label cell: a flex row of text and an optional extra (a MITRE chip or "home" tag) in secondary grey; `min-width: 0` allows its text to truncate.
The label text is cut off with an ellipsis instead of wrapping, using the standard trio of `overflow: hidden`, `text-overflow: ellipsis` and `white-space: nowrap`.
The 4px rounded track on `--s3`, placed in the `track` area and clipping its fill.
The fill bar: neutral `--t3` grey by default, with its width set inline as a share of the largest value, and `transform-origin: left` so bars.js can grow it from 0 to full with `scaleX`.

Only MEDIUM and HIGH bars switch to their risk colour (the only levels any caller passes; a CRITICAL variant nothing produced was removed). LOW and unlevelled bars stay grey, so colour picks out only what is risky.
The value cell: right-aligned medium-weight mono in white.
Section comment, then the gauge wrapper: up to 260px wide and centred, with `position: relative` so the number readout can be overlaid on the SVG.

The gauge SVG scales with its wrapper (`height: auto` keeps the 220×124 viewBox proportions), and `overflow: visible` stops the browser clipping anything past the viewBox, such as the "0" and "100" tick labels and the arc's glow.
The background track: the full semicircle in `--s3`, 14 units thick with round caps.
Four faint zone arcs (13% opacity), one per level and each coloured by its own `lvl-` class, show where LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH and CRITICAL begin on the dial.

The value arc: the same thickness with round caps, coloured `var(--lvl)` and given a glow by a `drop-shadow` filter mixing 45% of the level colour. gauge.js reveals it with `stroke-dasharray` and swaps its `lvl-` class as the animated value crosses each threshold, so the arc changes colour as it climbs.
The knob riding at the end of the arc: a dark `--s1` centre with a 3-unit ring in the level colour.
The tick marks at 0, 30, 60, 80 and 100 are thin faint strokes, and their numbers are 9.5px faint mono.
The readout is absolutely positioned across the bottom of the gauge, so the number sits inside the semicircle.
The big score: 46px Geist with tight negative letter-spacing for a display-style number (it also has `.num`, so its digits keep a fixed width while it counts up).
The caption under the number ("risk score", "peak score"): small uppercase letter-spaced mono in `--t3`.
Section comment, then `.waterfall` (the whole chart) and `.wf-rows` (the list of signal rows), both simple grids with 4px gaps.
Each row is a three-column grid: the signal label (at least 150px), the bar track (the widest, flexible column) and a fixed 92px weight column, with a 38px minimum height.
The label cell stacks its two lines with `display: grid`; `min-width: 0` lets the detail text truncate.
The signal name is medium-weight 12.5px; the detail line under it is small `--t3` text cut off with an ellipsis.

The track: an 18px rounded strip with an inset hairline (`box-shadow`) and a `repeating-linear-gradient` that draws a 1px `--s2` gridline every 10% of the width as a scale; `position: relative` lets the bar be placed inside it.

A step bar: absolutely positioned 3px in from the top and bottom and coloured `var(--lvl)`, with `left` and `width` set inline by waterfall.js so it starts where the running total stood and spans that signal's weight; these floating steps are what make it a waterfall. `transform-origin: left` lets the JS grow it in from the left.

Negative (risk-reducing) bars grow from the right, since they subtract, and are drawn as slate diagonal hatching (a 135° `repeating-linear-gradient` of 3px stripes and 3px gaps) with a slate outline, so they differ from positive bars in pattern as well as colour.
The weight cell (such as "+30" plus an optional MITRE chip): a right-aligned flex row in bold white mono.
Negative weights are slate instead of white.
The final "Risk score" row is separated by a dashed line above it, like the total line under a written sum.
The final score is 20px and takes the level colour of the result, because that cell carries its own `lvl-` class.
Section comment, then the map container: full width with `position: relative` so its layers can stack; worldmap.js sets its height from the map's aspect ratio.
The canvas (the dot-matrix land) and the SVG overlay (cities, arcs, pings) are both absolutely positioned to fill the container, so the overlay sits exactly on top of the canvas.
Inline SVGs clip to their own box by default; `overflow: visible` lets pulses, labels and arcs near the edges draw beyond it.
Travel arcs: unfilled curves, 1.3 units wide with round ends.

Arc types: `.plausible` trips are slate at 55% opacity, `.hostile` ones (origin flagged by IP reputation, speed not judged) are orange and dashed at 70%, and `.impossible` ones are thicker critical red with a red `drop-shadow` glow, so the most serious arcs stand out most.
A hovered arc thickens to 2.6 and becomes fully opaque; this rule comes after the type rules with equal specificity, so it overrides their width and opacity.
The "comet" that worldmap.js sends along up to three of the most recent impossible-travel arcs: a white dot with a red glow.

Each city is an SVG `g` group with a pointer cursor (clicking opens Events filtered by that city). SVG elements scale around the SVG's own origin by default, so `transform-box: fill-box` with `transform-origin: center` makes the entrance `scale` animation grow each city from its own centre instead of sweeping in from the top-left corner.
The city dot is filled with its level colour and outlined with a 1.5-unit `--bg` stroke that separates it from the dots and arcs beneath.
Low-risk cities use plain light grey (`--t2`) instead of slate, keeping colour for cities that carry real risk.

An invisible 10px-radius hit circle around each city that enlarges the pointer target. `fill: transparent` still counts as painted for SVG pointer events (`fill: none` would not), so it catches hovers and clicks.

City labels in small mono. `paint-order: stroke` draws the 3px `--bg`-coloured stroke before the fill, so the stroke becomes a dark halo around each letter instead of eating into it, keeping labels legible over dots and arcs.
Hovering a city outlines its dot in white.

The sonar ring around high-risk cities (peak score of 60 or more): an unfilled circle in the level colour looping the `mappulse` animation every 2.4s, with `transform-box: fill-box` so it scales around its own centre.
The one-off ripple drawn when a live event arrives; worldmap.js animates its radius and opacity in JS and removes it afterwards, so only its stroke is styled here.
The `mappulse` keyframes grow the ring to 4.2 times its size while fading it from 90% opacity to invisible.
Space between the map and the legend row below it.

The stats strip under the map: five equal columns with 1px gaps on a container whose background is the hairline colour. The cells cover that background, so only the gaps show through as thin dividers, a neat way to get internal borders without bordering each cell.
Each stat cell: padding on an `--s1` background, which hides the container's hairline colour everywhere except the gaps.
The stat label: block-level, tiny uppercase mono in the faintest grey, cut off with an ellipsis if the cell is narrow.
The stat value: 17px medium-weight mono.
Only HIGH and CRITICAL values (flagged-IP origins, impossible routes, the fastest implied speed) take their risk colour.
The legend: a wrapping flex row in small `--t3` text, where each item is an inline-flex pair of swatch and label 7px apart.
A line swatch: an 18px-wide, zero-height element whose 1.6px top border is the visible line.
The swatches copy the arc styles: `.plausible` slate, `.hostile` orange and dashed, `.impossible` red.
A 7px round swatch for "Risky city"; its colour (critical red) is set inline by `MAP_LEGEND()`.
